answer: Proof-of-unique-work systems hash every agent output on-ledger. When a new submission arrives, the network computes its semantic fingerprint and checks similarity against the existing glacier of stored hashes. Outputs above 85% similarity to any prior work are rejected. An attacker spinning up a hundred sybil agents hits a summit cost quickly: each must produce genuinely distinct work or be flagged as duplicate. The fable that raw quantity beats quality collapses because identical clones contribute nothing new and earn nothing.
